prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: hit while turning left in Sugar Land, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported knee injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1298; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling in the left-turn lane at an intersection in Sugar Land, Texas, when the collision occurred. Driver 1 stated that the vehicle was turning left when it was struck by Driver 2, whose vehicle was proceeding through the intersection. Driver 1 reported pain in the left knee at the scene. The Passenger, seated in the front passenger seat, was also present, and both the responding officer and independent witnesses confirmed that Driver 1 was inside the vehicle at the time of impact. Witness statements, scene photographs, and Driver 2's account all agree with Driver 1's description of how the crash happened. The damage to Driver 1's vehicle is consistent with a side impact of the force described, and the injury reported by Driver 1 is consistent with the kind of contact that would occur in this type of collision. A few older scratches were noted on the vehicle's rear bumper, which may predate this incident and were not considered part of the damage from this crash. Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy covering the vehicle involved.
